A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Augmented Mass-Spring hair-simulation work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation timings, coupling ablations, comparisons with other approaches, interaction demonstrations, and appendix parameter explorations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original simulation results and adds qualitative demonstrations of video-driven avatars and expanded roller-coaster simulations.

M1.justification: The AMS forces, integration algorithm, collision handling, sagging correction, and procedural growth remain unchanged. Section 4.3.2 adds a limited application pipeline that extracts head motion through video-based facial tracking and uses it to drive the simulator.

E1.justification: v3 adds a video-driven avatar scenario and expands the extreme-motion demonstration to long, short, and curly hairstyles. The existing captured-wig, strand, wisp, object-interaction, beard, wind, and grooming scenarios remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain MS, Hsu et al.'s hybrid Cosserat-MPM approach, LHS interpolation, CT2Hair-based interpolation, and geometric trimming. Newly cited neural methods and the facial-tracking component are not added comparison baselines.

E3.justification: Matched experiments retain the reported hardware, spring constants, 128-cubed grid, strand and particle counts, and comparison procedures. Added demonstrations introduce no specified measurement protocol. Figure 7's existing discrepancy between 128 guides in the caption and 2,048 in the text persists.

E4.justification: Figure 10 extends the qualitative extreme-force test across three hairstyle categories, and Section 4.3.2 adds a facial-tracking case study. The integrity/angular coupling ablations and appendix procedural-growth parameter explorations are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Simulation timings remain point values without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v3 reports new qualitative avatar-motion results in Figures 2 and 12 and replaces the original Figure 10 sequence with expanded results across three hairstyles. Table 1 and the wig-comparison timings remain unchanged, including AMS's reported 0.04 ms for 1,024 strands and 1.9 ms for 10,422 strands.

T1.justification: The force definitions, Euler linearization, banded-system decomposition, gravity-preloading derivation, and procedural-growth equations are retained. v1's Algorithmics section moves to supplementary Section B; the other appendix derivations are renumbered without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract's central claims about real-time dense simulation, stability, global-shape preservation, non-Hookean behavior, and editing remain. The introduction adds the contribution claim that integrating facial tracking enables user-controlled avatars with coherent hair motion.

C2.justification: v3 removes the dedicated argument that previous sagging corrections unrealistically return hair to its initial configuration. Figure 7 also strengthens its characterization to operation 'without artifacts.' The physical-accuracy limitation and appendix warning about biphasic forces affecting fidelity remain.

D1.justification: v3 removes v1's promise to release source code upon acceptance. Implementation language, hardware, numerical procedures, preprocessing, and parameter disclosures remain available. The PDFs do not establish a change in actual code availability.

R1.justification: The neural-related-work subsection adds Quaffure, HairStep, Neural Haircut, NeuWigs, and MonoHair; RetinaFace supports the new application. Bartle et al. disappears with the sagging discussion. The basic positioning relative to physics-based and neural approaches remains.

P1.justification: Targeted restructuring moves Algorithmics into the supplement and groups grooming and facial tracking under Applications. Section 3.1 brings existing appendix motivation into the main explanation, while captions and wording receive edits. Most of the original narrative remains.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially revised: two facial-tracking figures are added, and Figure 10 becomes a full-width, three-style roller-coaster montage. Existing comparisons are resized and rearranged, while Algorithm 1 and the non-Hookean curve move into the supplement. Table 1 retains its structure and contents.

improvement.justification: The tracking application and expanded Figure 10 provide broader qualitative evidence of practical use, while Section 3.1 makes the existing mechanism rationale easier to follow. Full technical derivations remain available. These are modest gains: quantitative validation is unchanged, and the source-code release commitment is removed.
